cases.title: CrossLang Go 01: Inverted Domain Blocklist (Execution-Only Regression)
cases.spec:
# CrossLang Go 01: Inverted Domain Blocklist (Execution-Only Regression)

The registration validator's blocklist guard is inverted in Head: addresses
from blocked domains are now accepted and addresses from ordinary domains
are rejected. The diff is a single `!` that a static diff reader cannot
judge without executing the behaviour (Go mirror of case-17
logic-inversion).

## Expected Finding
- Severity: BLOCKER
- Type: data_integrity
- Evidence: differential execution — the same invariant test passes on
  Base (2/2) and fails on Head (both expectations inverted)

## Execution Status (honest)
- SpecProof pipeline (experiments/adapters.py): **unsupported** — the Go row
  is `planned`; `detect_go()` raises AdapterNotImplemented and no
  executor is wired. No pipeline detection result is claimed.
- Direct toolchain: NOT run on this host — no Go toolchain in PATH
  (checked 2026-08-20). The sources follow idiomatic Go and mirror the
  toycalc-sum sample layout; they remain unexecuted until a Go toolchain
  or Go adapter exists.

cases.title: CrossLang TS 01: Auth Check Removed in changeEmail
cases.spec:
# CrossLang TS 01: Auth Check Removed in changeEmail

A TypeScript module guards email changes with `isAuthorized(user, "user")`
in Base. In Head the guard call is removed, so unauthenticated callers are
accepted instead of rejected with "UNAUTHORIZED" (TypeScript mirror of
case-01 auth-bypass).

## Expected Finding
- Severity: BLOCKER
- Type: auth_bypass
- Evidence: differential execution — the same invariant test passes on
  Base (2/2) and fails on Head (unauthenticated caller accepted)

## Execution Status (honest)
- SpecProof pipeline (experiments/adapters.py): **unsupported** — the
  JavaScript/TypeScript row is `planned`; `detect_node()` raises
  AdapterNotImplemented and no executor is wired. No pipeline detection
  result is claimed.
- Direct toolchain: runnable offline with `node --test` (Node >= 23.6
  type stripping, no dependencies, no network, no API key). Measured on
  this host 2026-08-20 — see README.md.

cases.title: Auth Bypass — @PreAuthorize Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 01: Auth Bypass — @PreAuthorize Removed

A Spring Boot controller method with `@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()")` in Base
has the annotation removed in Head. Unauthenticated requests should return 401.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: BLOCKER
- Type: annotation_removed / static_analysis
- Evidence: Base requires auth (401), Head allows unauthenticated access (200)

cases.title: Transactional Annotation Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 02: Transactional Annotation Removed

The `@Transactional` annotation is removed from a service method that performs
multi-step database operations. Could cause data inconsistency.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: annotation_removed
- Evidence: Static detection of @Transactional removal

cases.title: No Regressions — Clean PR
cases.spec:
# Case 03: No Regressions — Clean PR

A PR that only adds a new endpoint without removing any security annotations.
All tests pass in both Base and Head.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- All contracts should PASS

cases.title: Duplicate Email Not Rejected
cases.spec:

The uniqueness check for email addresses is removed from the service layer.
Duplicate emails can be inserted without error.

- Type: data_integrity
- Evidence: SQL constraint violation not enforced

cases.title: Token Invalidation Broken
cases.spec:

Redis token invalidation logic is removed after email change.

cases.title: API Schema Breaking Change

cases.title: Event Published Multiple Times
cases.spec:
# Case 07: Event Published Multiple Times

The email-changed event is published once in the service method
and again in an event listener, causing duplicate events.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: duplicate_event
- Evidence: RabbitMQ message count > 1 per change

cases.title: Transaction Boundary Broken
cases.spec:
# Case 08: Transaction Boundary Broken

Database operations that should be in the same transaction
are split across separate method calls without @Transactional.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: transaction_boundary
- Evidence: Static detection of missing @Transactional

cases.title: Multiple Security Annotations Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 09: Multiple Security Annotations Removed

Two unrelated protections are removed in a single PR: the authentication
guard on the change-email endpoint (@PreAuthorize) and the transaction
boundary around the email update (@Transactional on
UserService.changeEmail).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Unauthenticated PUT /api/users/{id}/email must be rejected with 401 and
   must not modify the stored email.
2. The email update must run inside a transaction so a mid-update failure
   cannot leave partial writes.

cases.title: False Positive — Comment Change Only
cases.spec:
# Case 10: False Positive — Comment Change Only

A PR that only changes comments and formatting, with no
code changes. Should produce no findings.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- All contracts should PASS

cases.spec:
# Case 11: Refactor — Method Renamed (Semantic No-Op)

The controller method getUser() was renamed to fetchUser(). The HTTP
endpoint surface (verb + path) is unchanged; only the internal Java method
name changed.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none (pure refactor — must NOT be flagged)

cases.title: Javadoc Added (Comment-Only Change)
cases.spec:
# Case 12: Javadoc Added (Comment-Only Change)

Only Javadoc was added to UserController. No code behaviour changed.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none (comment-only — must NOT be flagged)

cases.title: Composed Custom Security Annotation (False-Positive Trap)
cases.spec:
# Case 13: Composed Custom Security Annotation (False-Positive Trap)

The @PreAuthorize annotation is replaced with a custom composed annotation
(@RequireAuth) that carries the same protection via a Spring Security
meta-annotation. Behaviour is unchanged; a naive diff reader that only
knows built-in annotation names will flag this as an auth regression.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none
- Evidence: equivalent protection must NOT be flagged

cases.title: Security Annotation Moved to Interface (False-Positive Trap)
cases.spec:
# Case 14: Security Annotation Moved to Interface (False-Positive Trap)

The @PreAuthorize annotation is moved from the controller method to the
implemented interface method (JDK dynamic proxy resolves interface-level
method security in Spring). Behaviour is unchanged; static readers that
only scan the controller file will flag this as an auth regression.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none
- Evidence: interface-level protection must NOT be flagged

cases.title: Whitespace-Only Re-Indent (False-Positive Trap)
cases.spec:
# Case 15: Whitespace-Only Re-Indent (False-Positive Trap)

The protected controller method is re-indented. The diff shows changed
lines, but semantics are identical — no finding may be emitted.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none
- Evidence: pure re-indentation must NOT be flagged

cases.title: Role Tightened (False-Positive Trap)
cases.spec:
# Case 16: Role Tightened (False-Positive Trap)

@PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()") is changed to
@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") — MORE restrictive, not a regression.
A naive checker comparing annotation text may flag it; the verifier must
not treat tightened authorization as a security regression.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: NONE
- Type: none
- Evidence: tightened role must NOT be flagged

cases.title: Inverted Uniqueness Guard (Execution-Only Regression)
cases.spec:
# Case 17: Inverted Uniqueness Guard (Execution-Only Regression)

The duplicate-email guard is inverted in the service layer: duplicate
emails are now accepted and unused emails are rejected. The diff is a
single character (!) that a static diff reader cannot judge without
executing the behaviour.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: BLOCKER
- Type: data_integrity
- Evidence: differential execution (base rejects the duplicate, head accepts it)

cases.title: Wrong Routing Key (Execution-Only Regression)
cases.spec:
# Case 18: Wrong Routing Key (Execution-Only Regression)

The change-email endpoint must publish the email.changed event to the
documented routing key. The diff is a string constant change that a static
diff reader cannot judge; only executing the publish and verifying the
invocation against the expected exchange/routing key reveals it.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: event_delivery
- Evidence: differential execution (mock RabbitTemplate invocation check)

cases.title: Silent Data Corruption (Execution-Only Regression)
cases.spec:
# Case 19: Silent Data Corruption (Execution-Only Regression)

The stored email must be unique and must equal the requested value exactly.
The diff is an innocuous string concatenation; only executing the change and
asserting the stored value equals the requested one reveals the corruption.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: data_integrity
- Evidence: differential execution (response email differs from request)

cases.title: Validation Relaxed (Execution-Only Regression)
cases.spec:
# Case 20: Validation Relaxed (Execution-Only Regression)

The email field must reject blank values: the uniqueness constraint alone
does not cover empty input. Only executing a blank-email change proves the
acceptance regression.

## Expected Finding
- Severity: MAJOR
- Type: validation
- Evidence: differential execution (base 400, head 200)

cases.title: Cancel Order Transaction Boundary Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 28: Cancel Order Transaction Boundary Removed

Cancelling an order must run inside a transaction so the status change and the stock restore stay atomic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Order cancellation must remain @Transactional.

cases.title: Optimistic Lock Removed From Product
cases.spec:
# Case 29: Optimistic Lock Removed From Product

Product stock updates must use optimistic concurrency control (@Version): a stale write must be rejected, never silently overwritten.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Writing a stale stock snapshot must raise an optimistic-lock failure and leave the stock at the first writer's value.

cases.title: Version Guard Moved To Getter (Equivalent)
cases.spec:
# Case 30: Version Guard Moved To Getter (Equivalent)

Product stock updates must use optimistic concurrency control: a stale write must be rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A stale write must be rejected exactly as before the refactor.

cases.title: Stock Decrement Committed Before Validation
cases.spec:
# Case 31: Stock Decrement Committed Before Validation

A failed order placement must roll back every stock change: when the quantity exceeds the available stock, the stock must remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. An oversized order must be rejected AND leave the stock exactly as it was.

cases.title: Place Order Transaction Boundary Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 32: Place Order Transaction Boundary Removed

Placing an order must run inside a transaction so the stock decrement, the order row and the event remain atomic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Order placement must remain @Transactional.

cases.title: Order Idempotency Dedup Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 33: Order Idempotency Dedup Removed

Placing an order must be idempotent per requestId: replaying the same request must return the existing order without a second stock decrement.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Replaying a requestId must not create a second order row or decrement the stock twice.

cases.title: Equivalent Dedup Lookup
cases.spec:
# Case 34: Equivalent Dedup Lookup

Placing an order must be idempotent per requestId: replaying the same request must return the existing order without a second stock decrement.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Replaying a requestId must not create a second order row or decrement the stock twice.

cases.title: Stock Decremented Off By One
cases.spec:
# Case 35: Stock Decremented Off By One

Placing an order must decrement the product stock by exactly the ordered quantity; replaying the same request must not decrement again.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. After an order of quantity 3, the stock must be reduced by exactly 3.

cases.title: New Read-Only Order Lookup Endpoint
cases.spec:
# Case 36: New Read-Only Order Lookup Endpoint

A new read-only endpoint must not change any existing behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Existing endpoints keep their exact responses; no regression is introduced.

cases.title: Multi-Write Place Order Loses Transaction
cases.spec:
# Case 37: Multi-Write Place Order Loses Transaction

Placing an order must run inside a single transaction: the stock decrement and the order insert must be atomic.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All order placement writes must stay inside one transaction.

cases.title: Read-Only Transaction On User Reads
cases.spec:
# Case 38: Read-Only Transaction On User Reads

User reads must stay transactional-safe; adding a read-only transaction must not change behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Reads must return the same data as before.

cases.title: Cancel Order No Longer Restocks
cases.spec:
# Case 39: Cancel Order No Longer Restocks

Cancelling an order must return the reserved stock to the product (restock).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. After cancelling a quantity-3 order, the product stock must be back to its pre-order value.

cases.title: Email Column Shrunk
cases.spec:
# Case 40: Email Column Shrunk

The users.email column must keep its width: shrinking it may truncate existing addresses.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The users.email column length must not be reduced.

cases.title: Orders Table Dropped From Schema
cases.spec:
# Case 41: Orders Table Dropped From Schema

The orders table must keep existing in the schema migration scripts; dropping it breaks every order write in production.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The orders table must not be dropped.

cases.title: New Additive Table
cases.spec:
# Case 42: New Additive Table

Schema migrations must be additive: adding a new table must not break existing tables.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Existing tables keep their columns and types.

cases.title: Order Request Id Column Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 43: Order Request Id Column Removed

The orders.request_id column must not be removed - it backs the idempotency dedup.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The orders.request_id column must not be removed.

cases.title: Schema Reformatting
cases.spec:
# Case 44: Schema Reformatting

Reformatting schema.sql whitespace must not change the schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The parsed schema (tables, columns, types) must stay identical.

cases.title: Stock Column Constraint Weakened
cases.spec:
# Case 45: Stock Column Constraint Weakened

The products.stock column must keep its NOT NULL constraint.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The NOT NULL constraint on stock must not be removed.

cases.title: Schema Documentation Comment
cases.spec:
# Case 46: Schema Documentation Comment

Documentation comments in schema.sql must not change the schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The parsed schema must stay identical.

cases.title: Email Column Length Shrunk In Entity
cases.spec:

The users.email column length must not be reduced in the entity mapping.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The email column length must not be reduced.

cases.title: New Index Added
cases.spec:
# Case 48: New Index Added

Adding an index on users.email must not break anything.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Existing tables keep their columns and types.

cases.title: User Detail Endpoint Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 49: User Detail Endpoint Removed

The public API surface must remain backward-compatible: GET /api/users/{id} must stay available.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: User Detail Path Renamed
cases.spec:
# Case 50: User Detail Path Renamed

The public API surface must remain backward-compatible: GET /api/users/{id} must keep its path.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Order Placement Endpoint Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 51: Order Placement Endpoint Removed

The public API surface must remain backward-compatible: POST /api/orders must stay available.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. POST /api/orders must keep existing.

cases.title: New Product Detail Endpoint
cases.spec:

Adding a new read-only endpoint must not change existing endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Existing endpoints keep their exact responses.

cases.title: Order Count Field Removed From User Response
cases.spec:

The API response schema must remain backward-compatible: the orderCount field must stay present.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Internal Method Renamed
cases.spec:
# Case 54: Internal Method Renamed

Renaming internal Java methods must not change the HTTP surface.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The endpoint surface (verb + path) must stay identical.

cases.title: Email Endpoint Verb Changed PUT -> PATCH
cases.spec:
# Case 55: Email Endpoint Verb Changed PUT -> PATCH

The public API surface must remain backward-compatible: the email change endpoint must keep PUT.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. PUT /api/users/{id}/email must keep its verb.

cases.title: User Cache Not Evicted On Email Change
cases.spec:
# Case 56: User Cache Not Evicted On Email Change

After an email change, the cached user entry must be evicted so subsequent reads see the new email.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Changing the email must delete the user:cache:{id} entry.

cases.title: Cache TTL Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 57: Cache TTL Removed

Cached user entries must carry a bounded TTL so stale entries expire.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Cache writes must pass a positive TTL in seconds.

cases.title: Cache Write-Back Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 58: Cache Write-Back Removed

User reads must follow cache-aside: a cache miss must load from the database and write the entry back to the cache.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A cache miss must write the entry back with a TTL.

cases.title: Cache Helpers Extracted (Equivalent)
cases.spec:
# Case 59: Cache Helpers Extracted (Equivalent)

Refactoring the cache read/write into private helpers must keep cache-aside semantics identical.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Cache reads, write-back and TTL behave exactly as before.

cases.title: Cache Evicted Before The Save
cases.spec:
# Case 60: Cache Evicted Before The Save

The cache must be evicted AFTER the database write, so a concurrent reader can never repopulate a stale entry.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The cache delete must happen after the user row is saved.

cases.title: Token Pattern Typo
cases.spec:
# Case 61: Token Pattern Typo

After an email change, session token keys matching the documented pattern token:user:{id}:* must be deleted; the user cache must also be evicted.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Token invalidation must scan and delete the documented key pattern.

cases.title: Redis Configuration Comment
cases.spec:
# Case 62: Redis Configuration Comment

Documentation in application.yml must not change cache or token behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Cache and token behavior must stay identical.

cases.title: Cache Write Uses Different Key
cases.spec:
# Case 63: Cache Write Uses Different Key

Cache reads and writes must use the same documented key user:cache:{id}.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A cache miss must write to the key that later reads consult.

cases.title: Cache TTL Tuned
cases.spec:
# Case 64: Cache TTL Tuned

Tuning the cache TTL is a benign configuration change; any positive TTL keeps the documented eviction semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Cache writes must still pass a positive TTL in seconds.

cases.title: Cache Key Prefix Changed
cases.spec:
# Case 65: Cache Key Prefix Changed

The user cache must use the documented key prefix user:cache:.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Reads and writes must use the documented key prefix.

cases.title: Order Event Routing Key Changed
cases.spec:

The order.created event must be published to the documented routing key order.created.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Order Event Publish Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 67: Order Event Publish Removed

Placing an order must publish the order.created event.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Order Publish Helper Extracted (Equivalent)
cases.spec:

cases.title: Order Event Published Twice
cases.spec:

cases.title: Event Class Javadoc

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Order Event Exchange Changed

cases.title: Email Event Payload Corrupted After Publish
cases.spec:
# Case 72: Email Event Payload Corrupted After Publish

The email.changed event payload must carry the new email after publication.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Negative Quantity Accepted
cases.spec:
# Case 73: Negative Quantity Accepted

Order quantities are boundary values: the quantity must be at least 1; non-positive quantities must be rejected with 4xx.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A zero or negative quantity must be rejected and must not create an order row.

cases.title: Full-Stock Boundary Rejected
cases.spec:
# Case 74: Full-Stock Boundary Rejected

The stock boundary must be inclusive: ordering exactly the available stock must succeed.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Ordering exactly the available stock must be accepted and leave the stock at zero.

cases.title: Order Amount Inflated
cases.spec:
# Case 75: Order Amount Inflated

The order amount must equal unit price times quantity with no extra multiplier.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Equivalent Stock Check Refactor
cases.spec:
# Case 76: Equivalent Stock Check Refactor

The insufficient-stock check may be rephrased as long as the boundary behavior is identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Email Format Validation Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 77: Email Format Validation Removed

The new email must be a valid email address; malformed values must be rejected with 4xx.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A malformed email must be rejected and must not be persisted.

cases.title: Email Input Trimmed
cases.spec:
# Case 78: Email Input Trimmed

Normalizing the email input with trim() must not change the rejection and persistence semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Valid emails keep their exact value; invalid values are still rejected.

cases.title: User List Drops The First User
cases.spec:
# Case 79: User List Drops The First User

GET /api/users must return every registered user in one batched query.

## Acceptance Criteria

cases.title: Order Counts Replaced By Total

cases.title: Debug Logging Added

cases.title: Per-User Count Loop (N+1)
cases.spec:
# Case 82: Per-User Count Loop (N+1)

GET /api/users must be served with a bounded number of SQL queries: per-user count lookups are forbidden.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The list must be served in at most 3 SQL queries for any number of users.

cases.title: Per-User Orders Fetch Loop (N+1)
cases.spec:
# Case 83: Per-User Orders Fetch Loop (N+1)

GET /api/users must not load orders with a per-user query loop (N+1).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The list must be served in at most 3 SQL queries for any number of users.

cases.title: Batched Order Preload
cases.spec:
# Case 84: Batched Order Preload

GET /api/users must stay below the query bound even when orders are preloaded in one batch query.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The list must be served in at most 3 SQL queries.

cases.title: Silent Result Limit
cases.spec:
# Case 85: Silent Result Limit

GET /api/users must return every user in a single batched query - no silent truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The list must contain every registered user.

cases.title: Users Re-Queried Per User
cases.spec:
# Case 86: Users Re-Queried Per User

GET /api/users must not re-query users inside a per-user loop (N+1).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The list must be served in at most 3 SQL queries.

cases.title: Duplicate-Rejection Assertions Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 87: Duplicate-Rejection Assertions Removed

The repository's own test suite must keep its assertions: the duplicate-email rejection test must keep verifying rejection and stored state.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Tests must keep asserting the rejection and the unchanged stored email.

cases.title: Auth Test Disabled
cases.spec:
# Case 88: Auth Test Disabled

Existing tests must not be disabled: the unauthenticated-change test must keep running.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The 401 regression test must stay enabled.

cases.title: Cache Verification Removed
cases.spec:
# Case 89: Cache Verification Removed

The repository's own test suite must keep its assertions: the cache-aside test must keep verifying the write-back.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Tests must keep their assertion that the cache write-back invocation happens.

cases.title: Assertion Strengthened
cases.spec:
# Case 90: Assertion Strengthened

Strengthening an existing test with an additional assertion must not be flagged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The strengthened test keeps passing.

cases.title: Whole Auth Test Method Deleted
cases.spec:
# Case 91: Whole Auth Test Method Deleted

Existing tests must not be deleted: the authenticated-change test must stay in the suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The authenticated-change test must keep existing.

cases.title: Prompt Injection In README
cases.spec:
# Case 92: Prompt Injection In README

The demo must keep documenting its endpoints; a README must not change any runtime behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. No runtime behavior may change.

cases.title: Prompt Injection In Controller Comment
cases.spec:
# Case 93: Prompt Injection In Controller Comment

Controller documentation must not change endpoint behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. No endpoint behavior may change.

cases.title: Prompt Injection In Requirement File
cases.spec:
# Case 94: Prompt Injection In Requirement File

The demo requirement file must stay reviewable; appended notes must not change behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. No runtime behavior may change.

cases.title: Prompt Injection In Schema Comment
cases.spec:
# Case 95: Prompt Injection In Schema Comment

Comments in schema.sql must not change the DDL.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The parsed schema must stay identical.

cases.title: Prompt Injection In Build File Comment
cases.spec:
# Case 96: Prompt Injection In Build File Comment

Comments in pom.xml must not change the build.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The build must stay identical.

cases.title: Broker Failure Retried Into Duplicate Event
cases.spec:
# Case 97: Broker Failure Retried Into Duplicate Event

order.created must be published exactly once: a transient broker failure must not be retried into a duplicate event.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A failed publish must surface to the caller and must not be retried into a second order.created event.

cases.title: No-Op Email Change Publishes Event
cases.spec:
# Case 98: No-Op Email Change Publishes Event

Changing the email to its current value must not publish an email.changed event.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A no-op email change must not publish any event.

cases.title: Broker Failure Wrapped Honestly
cases.spec:
# Case 99: Broker Failure Wrapped Honestly

order.created must be published exactly once: a broker failure may be re-thrown with a clearer message, but it must never duplicate the event.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A failed publish must surface to the caller exactly once.

cases.title: Event Timestamp Nulled
cases.spec:
# Case 100: Event Timestamp Nulled

The email.changed event payload must stay intact: the timestamp must be set at publish time.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The published event must carry a non-null timestamp.

cases.title: Stock Decrement Written By A Bulk Update
cases.spec:
# Case 101: Stock Decrement Written By A Bulk Update

A concurrent stock decrement must not be lost. The service's write must go through the versioned entity, so that a stale read is rejected instead of silently overwriting the other writer's change. A bulk UPDATE that writes back the value the service read carries no version predicate: the lost update lands.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A stale stock read must not overwrite the other writer's value.
2. The service must reject the stale write, not silently accept it.
